headline: With one dispute already on file, the gold gives provisional credit to only the first two new disputes filed, which depends on an unstated counting rule and on filing order; one refund type is also left to guesswork.

issues.summary: One dispute is on file (dsp_ed3ab3dce038, submitted 09/20/2025). Four new disputes have a provisional-eligible reason. Gold credits only Grainger and Uline and denies American Airlines ($342.50 fraud) and Best Buy ($189.99 duplicate). That holds only if disputes filed in this conversation count toward criterion 4, which doc_015 leaves open.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015: "Eligibility Criteria — Customer is ELIGIBLE for provisional credit if ALL of the following are true: ... 4. Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months"
initial_state.agent_data.transaction_disputes.dsp_ed3ab3dce038: submitted_at "09/20/2025", status "APPROVED"; replayed get_user_dispute_history_7291 shows exactly this 1 record
gold[7] txn_25e23705f61f Grainger $523.45 true; gold[8] txn_fd4c3871654e Uline $412.34 true; gold[9] txn_a1b2c3d4e503 American Airlines $342.50 false; gold[10] txn_a1b2c3d4e510 Best Buy $189.99 false

Other criteria hold for all four: cc_01f21c9970_gold opened 06/15/2024 and cc_01f21c9970_bgold 09/01/2024 (both over 60 days); amounts within $25 to $10,000 (Premium Tier); duplicates contacted_merchant true
tools.py file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 stores eligible_for_provisional_credit verbatim and sets provisional_credit_given to the same value
Replay: gold with gold[9] eligible true -> verified match False: table 'transaction_disputes' differs
issues.why_it_matters: Under the snapshot reading (1 prior dispute, which is not more than 2), all four qualify, and an agent following it fails. Only the cumulative reading (1 then 2, the third new filing is denied) reproduces the gold.
issues.suggested_fix: State in doc_015 that disputes filed earlier in the same interaction count toward criterion 4, or mark all four reason-eligible disputes true.

issues.summary: Under the cumulative reading, the two remaining slots go to whichever disputes are filed first, of any reason. The gold needs Grainger and Uline filed first. The customer reveals this priority only 'If the agent mentions provisional credit or asks about it'.
evidence: user script step 6: "The Grainger and Uline charges are the biggest ones hurting my business cash flow right now... Please prioritize those if there's any limit."

Computation: filing in the customer's listed order (Gold card: AA, Best Buy, PECO, Spotify; then Business: Uline, Grainger, Best Buy, Comcast) under the cumulative reading gives eligible = {AA $342.50, Best Buy $189.99}, the opposite of gold[7..10]
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that applies the cap correctly but never raises provisional credit, or files in the customer's order, records the wrong two disputes as credited.
issues.suggested_fix: Have the customer state the priority up front, or document a deterministic rule such as largest-first for allocating a capped allowance.

issues.summary: The script never states a resolution type. For the Comcast refund_never_processed charge ($189.99), the customer was 'promised a partial refund', but the gold records full_refund. The partial amount is unknown, and doc_014 has no default.
evidence: script: "Comcast $189.99 on 10/30/2025 - REFUND NOT PROCESSED. You downgraded your business internet plan and were promised a partial refund weeks ago."
doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_014: "resolution_requested (string) - Ask user what resolution they want." / "'partial_refund': Partial amount (must also provide partial_refund_amount)"
Replay: gold with gold[14] partial_refund (amount 50) -> verified match False: table 'transaction_disputes' differs
issues.why_it_matters: When asked, the customer simulator may well ask for a partial refund, which the script's facts support. The agent would then file partial_refund and fail. This is an unscripted refund-type choice with no document default.
issues.suggested_fix: Script the resolution for each dispute (e.g. 'full refund for all except a $24.56 partial refund on PECO'), or change the Comcast story to a full-refund case.

solution_check: Verify the customer and read the dispute history (1 approved dispute from 09/20/2025; a required gold read). Give get_card_last_4_digits for both cards (gold 1652, bgold 0581). File 8 disputes with keep_active, the scripted reasons and contact answers, noticed 11/14/2025, and PECO as partial_refund 24.56. The fixed fields match the gold. The provisional flags match only under the cumulative reading of criterion 4 with Grainger and Uline filed first. Comcast's full_refund depends on how the simulator answers.
prior_note: The prior Blocker on the provisional-credit cap persists in the data. I rate it Major because the gold follows a doc-supported cumulative reading and the customer's priority line supplies the order. The Comcast refund-type issue is a new Major.
notes: The injected prior dispute is internally inconsistent: purchase_date 10/02/2025 is after issue_noticed_date 09/15/2025 and submitted_at 09/20/2025. This is cosmetic, because criterion 4 counts by filing date. Spotify $10.99 is under the $25 minimum and its reason is ineligible either way. PECO partial_refund 24.56 follows from 'They overcharged you by $24.56'. The verified scorer still requires get_user_dispute_history_7291 to be called. Author notes cite a hidden 'provisional_credit_max_disputes_in_period = 3' setting that appears nowhere agent-visible; the gold flags agree with the cumulative reading of doc_015.
